# Profile-driven diagram theming

## 1. Select the design profile

Delegate palette curation to the design-profiles skill when it is available.
Resolve an explicit profile or the project's `.design-profiles/.default-profile` before authoring colors.
Without a project profile, use this skill's prebuilt `themes/osakanights/themes.css` and matching `design-tokens.json` under `resources/`.
The fallback is generated by design-profiles; do not maintain another palette here.

```bash
bun run .claude/skills/richdocs/vendor/mermaidjs-diagrams/scripts/design_profile.ts status
bun run .claude/skills/richdocs/vendor/mermaidjs-diagrams/scripts/design_profile.ts palette --mode light
bun run .claude/skills/richdocs/vendor/mermaidjs-diagrams/scripts/design_profile.ts palette --mode dark
```

The reader returns baked values; it does not regenerate a Golden Walk or invent theme colors.
Request a profile change from design-profiles when a required theme role is absent.

## 2. Encode meaningful categories

Assign the next `--categorical-HH` slot to each meaningful category in a fixed order.
Reuse that assignment across overview, detail, sequence and data-model views.
Choose categories from actual topics, teams, phases, owners, systems or responsibilities.
Do not assign a different hue to every node or attach universal meanings to palette slots.
Keep labels and boundaries explicit so color reinforces meaning without becoming the only cue.

`HH` is the zero-padded hue-family identifier `01` through `10`, not a literal angle.
The Golden Walk is already computed in the profile.
Hue spacing does not guarantee perceptual separation or accessible contrast.
When categories exceed the available slots, group them or split views instead of cycling colors.

## 3. Distinguish related subcategories

Each categorical hue has five `--palette-HH-S` shades, with `S` from `1` through `5`.
Shade 1 is the category root; successive shades are darker in the generated recipe.
Use shades within a family for related subcategories and keep their meanings consistent across views.
Use only the shades required by the model.
Do not invent subcategories to consume every shade.
Reserve status roles for status rather than treating a category slot as success or failure.

The [assignment patterns](color_palette_recipes.md) describe category roles without defining alternative palettes.

## 4. Resolve colors before emitting Mermaid

GitHub Mermaid fences cannot load the theme CSS or evaluate `var(...)`.
Use the profile's baked sRGB fallbacks from `design_profile.ts palette`, or a color-aware converter for selected OKLCH CSS values.
Never estimate a hex value or paste unresolved CSS variables into Mermaid source.
Use the styling syntax supported by the selected diagram family.

Put explicit style values and relevant Mermaid theme variables in the source so the linter can audit them.
An external `mmdc` configuration or HTML provider does not rewrite that source.
Do not claim a lint verdict covers styling supplied only by an external renderer.
For fixed Markdown styles, select fills and foregrounds that read together on both host canvases.
Render light and dark locally before publishing the fence itself.

## 5. Style compound boundaries

Assign each meaningful boundary the hue family used by its members.
For each target canvas, mix 16 percent category color with 84 percent canvas, channel by channel in encoded sRGB.
Round the mixed channels to integers and emit an opaque fill.
Use a solid 2px border in a readable same-family shade and the theme foreground for the title.
The categorical root itself may lack enough border contrast; select another shade when needed.
Keep leaf nodes visually distinct from their container.

Emit an explicit `style groupId ...` statement for every named Mermaid subgraph with a known category.
For Cytoscape, a compound has children referencing its ID through `data.parent`; `data.category` selects category styling.
Apply the same tint recipe to tagged compounds at full background opacity.
Keep titles top-aligned with space above child nodes.

Check each nested group against its immediate parent surface as well as the canvas.
Do not stack translucent fills without accounting for accumulated opacity.
Five repeated 16 percent fills accumulate to about 58 percent effective opacity.
Use opaque resolved tints per surface, or transparent inner structural boundaries when a single fixed Markdown style must span hosts.
In HTML, select the matching mode's tokens and rerender Mermaid from source when the provider changes.

## 6. Style complete entity tables

Keep every in-scope entity, relationship and attribute when applying a theme.
Do not remove attributes to silence an unresolved-theme diagnostic.
Resolve entity headers and both alternating row backgrounds before selecting a fixed foreground.
Use the compound recipe for headers and even rows; use the canvas for odd rows.
Choose a same-family border and a foreground that contrasts with both fills in both modes.

Set explicit `rowOdd` and `rowEven` when the selected theme leaves row colors unresolved.
Use Mermaid's native `base` theme when another theme flattens row alternation.
Verify the emitted SVG's precedence between entity fills and row variables.
Use native theme variables and class styles rather than unauditable CSS overrides.

## 7. Color sequence participants and groups

Apply the shared categorical mapping to meaningful participant families.
Use supported per-participant styles, or labelled native `box` groups around related declarations.
Resolve box colors to supported `rgb(...)` or `rgba(...)` values.
Do not copy flowchart `classDef` or `style` syntax into a sequence diagram without verifying support.
Use `rect` for execution phases; it does not replace participant-category grouping.

Check participant labels, group titles, messages, lifelines, activations, notes and alternative-frame text against every surface they occupy.
Use wrapping and participant-width settings when labels overflow their boxes.
Demonstrate renderer limitations rather than declaring semantic coloring complete after a parse-only check.

## 8. Validate the source and both rendered modes

```bash
bunx @jpeakai/remark-lint-slopstopper SOURCE.md
```

The standalone CLI enables recommended Markdown rules, prose policies and Mermaid policies.
Use `--mermaid-only` while isolating diagrams; it still checks Markdown structure.
Custom canvases use native remark configuration, described in [contrast tooling](contrast_tooling.md).
Slopstopper 0.1.2 has no MkDocs host-profile switch and does not certify CSS-forced labels.
Inspect host-rendered labels and borders in both modes; see [host-themed rendering](color_host_themed_renderers.md).

Run `mmdc` on each final diagram in both target modes and inspect the resulting PNGs yourself.
Keep verification artifacts in ignored scratch storage such as `tmp/diagrams/`.
Review nested fills, titles, label clipping, routing, row alternation and contrast at a readable scale.
Iterate on the source and regenerate after every correction.
Publish native Mermaid fences, including inside existing descriptive `<details>` when appropriate.
Do not replace them with images, base64 data or a new disclosure that merely hides the source.
